description: The figure is a two-level donut chart intended to show the distribution of two related categorical measures, with an outer ring labeled “(Outer)” representing standard-deviation (Std) categories and an inner ring labeled “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” representing maximum-ambiguity (Max) categories; the outer ring contains 4 slices and the inner ring contains 3 slices. In the outer ring, four blue-toned segments are shown with percentage labels on the ring: a dark teal slice labeled “Std: 0.0” at approximately 49.0%, a medium-dark blue slice labeled “Std: 0.47” at approximately 39.0%, a brighter blue slice labeled “Std: 0.82” at approximately 5.0%, and a light bright-blue slice labeled “Std: 0.94” at approximately 7.0%. In the inner ring, three lighter blue segments are labeled with percentages: “Max: 1” at approximately 47.7% (medium light blue), “Max: 2” at approximately 38.0% (lighter blue), and “Max: 3” at approximately 14.2% (very pale blue). The chart includes two legends on the right mapping colors to the outer and inner labels, percentage values are printed directly on the slices, and no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; the segments appear arranged around the circle without an explicitly indicated ordering rule.
